page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-8 is a flexible general-purpose virtual machine shape configured with 1 physical core (2 vCPUs) and 8.0 GB of memory. It runs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J45 processor with a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. Compute resources are provided via dedicated CPU allocation, with simultaneous multithreading active across two hardware threads per physical core.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, having 0 GPUs and requiring remote block volumes for persistent filesystems. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The 1:4 ratio of vCPUs to system RAM (4.0 GB of memory per vCPU) matches standard general-purpose resource allocations.

Without local NVMe drives, I/O performance relies on network-attached storage infrastructure. However, the dedicated physical core avoids CPU contention typical of burstable or shared-core tiers, offering predictable execution for lightweight web services, microservices, development environments, and small automation tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 1 dedicated physical core providing 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for filesystem persistence, and does not include GPU acceleration. Networking provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because CPU resources are dedicated rather than burstable or shared, the shape provides steady execution without neighbor contention. This setup makes the VM.Standard.E6.Flex.1-8 practical for entry-level general workloads, including small web servers, internal tools, light background processing, API gateways, and software testing environments.
